raw_response:
I've been farming this land in Quzhou for 40 years, and at 64 I know every corner of my 10.1 mu. It's just me and my wife now, so I have to be smart with labor. I grow only cotton — it's what this soil is good for, and after four decades I can read the crop like a book.

This spring, I'll plant my cotton around late April when the soil warms up. I'll use an improved variety like Guoxinmian — I've tried others, but these seeds give me reliable bolls and good disease resistance. I'll put down about 3 jin of seed per mu. Before sowing, I'll run the rotary tiller to break up the stubble and prepare a fine seedbed. That's what most of us do here, and it works.

For fertilizer, I've learned you can't starve cotton if you want a decent yield. I'll put down a compound fertilizer as my basal dose — roughly 18 kg of nitrogen, 6 kg of phosphorus, and 6 kg of potassium per mu. Then I'll topdress with urea once during flowering to give the plants a push when they need it most. My well gives me reliable water, so I'll irrigate three times: right after sowing to help germination, at the flowering stage, and during boll formation. That extra water at the right time is why my yields stay steady when the rain fails.

Pests are the biggest enemy. I'll spray about 14 times through the season — mostly insecticide for bollworm and aphids, but I'll throw in herbicide early and a plant growth regulator to keep the plants from getting too leggy. It's a lot of trips across the field, but if you skip sprays, you lose the crop. With my experience and the well irrigation, I expect to harvest around 220 kg of seed cotton per mu by early October. That's a realistic target — not the best year I've ever had, but a solid, dependable one.
